Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Summary:  50-year-old woman with T2DM and HTN presents with 5–6 days of dry cough (no sputum), rhinorrhea, subjective chills, myalgias, fatigue, and transient early diarrhea now resolved. No chest pain, no baseline dyspnea, ears normal, appetite acceptable. On metformin and lisinopril. Former smoker; partner asymptomatic. No vitals or exam documented.  
- Working diagnosis:  Acute viral respiratory infection (upper respiratory infection/viral bronchitis). Supported by short duration, constellation of upper respiratory and systemic symptoms, and absence of red flags (per transcript and DDx).  
- Relevant differentials (consistent with DDx):  
  - COVID-19 (plausible given dry cough, chills, myalgias, fatigue, and initial diarrhea; no testing performed).  
  - Influenza (myalgias/chills and cough compatible; fever not documented).  
  - Community-acquired pneumonia less likely currently (no dyspnea, chest pain, or productive cough; no vitals/exam suggesting pneumonia).  
  - ACE inhibitor–induced cough less likely (acute onset with viral prodrome).  
- Plan (as discussed):  
  - Rest and maintain hydration.  
  - Use regular paracetamol/acetaminophen for symptom relief (dose not documented).  
  - Consider taking 1–2 days off work to reduce infectious risk and allow recovery.  
  - Safety net: return in 2–3 days if not improving; sooner if breathing worsens. If persistent feverishness and cough not improving, clinician to reassess and consider antibiotics.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Acute viral respiratory infection (common cold/viral bronchitis) — High likelihood: Short course of dry cough, rhinorrhea, chills, myalgias, and fatigue without dyspnea or chest pain fits a self-limited viral illness.  
- COVID-19 — Medium likelihood: Dry cough, chills, myalgias, fatigue, and initial diarrhea are compatible; no testing performed.  
- Influenza — Medium likelihood: Systemic myalgias/chills with cough support this; fever not documented but not required.
